boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Wauhatchie record (October 28–29, 1863) in Reopening the Tennessee River [October 1863]. The October 27 Brown's Ferry landing, which the live page gives as another name, falls before the frozen interval; its losses are not added. The attack on Geary and the fight for the hill near Howard's camp are both within the night. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the XI Corps and the 2nd Division, XII Corps, against Hood's Division, without counts; the live field reads zero. Cist says the enemy attacked Geary in greatly superior numbers. Bratton names the six regiments of Jenkins' brigade he put in and says the enemy's line of fire was not more than 300 or 400 yards long.
claims.rationale: No count is inspected; relative claims are not counts. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Cist says Geary's division camped near Wauhatchie, some three miles up Lookout Valley from Howard's camp, so the two camps could not keep communication or form one line, and that Orland Smith's brigade charged a hill almost inaccessible by daylight to reach Confederate intrenchments. claims.value: NPS says the attack, scheduled for 10 p.m., was delayed by confusion until midnight, and that Geary's division was surprised. Bratton says his skirmishers found commotion in the Union camp and could not tell whether it was preparation to receive or to leave. Cist says a regiment ordered by Howard to hold the Chattanooga road skirmished with the Confederate advance about midnight.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from a summary and interested accounts; no message log inspected.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says the Confederates fell back to Lookout Mountain as Union reinforcements arrived. Cist says the Confederates were repulsed and the Union held the field. Bratton says his brigade withdrew in order, bringing away most of its wounded, and was the last to recross the creek.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 828 (US 420; CS 408); the live field reads 572 (US 216; CS 356). Cist gives the Union loss as 76 killed, 339 wounded and 22 missing, 437 in all, says the Confederate loss is unknown, and says Geary buried 153 Confederates and 100 prisoners were taken. Bratton's inclosure totals 31 killed, 286 wounded and 39 missing, 356, for Jenkins' brigade; one row (Palmetto Sharpshooters, '6 35 44') lacks a figure in OCR.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Bratton's brigade total equals the live Confederate figure; the Brown's Ferry losses of October 27 are not added.

open_questions: Hooker's, Geary's, Howard's, Longstreet's and Law's reports, the court of inquiry and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Cist is an interested Union staff history. Bratton's report, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXI, Part 1, is an interested account by the colonel commanding Jenkins' brigade; the frozen Confederate commander, Jenkins, has no report in the inspected list. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
